summary: Kickoff scoping call for a 4-week POC to validate unit economics for Cygnus Analytics' new summarization and search assistant. Core goals: validate per-token costs with batching/caching, verify P95 latency targets under production-like traffic, and deliver a benchmark spreadsheet with projected monthly costs. Customer prefers hosted API but needs clarity on VPC/KMS for sensitive data. Preliminary budget constraint: <$18k/month for inference. Agreed next steps: SOW + pricing, benchmark harness, sample prompts, architecture review.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 11:00 PT / Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Solutions); Maya Ortiz (Cygnus PM), Jamal Reed (Cygnus Eng), Kelsey Park (Cygnus FinOps)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from Redwood, today we're going to map out the POC scope — economics, benchmarks, and timeline. Samir's going to drive the technical bits.
[00:18] Maya Ortiz: Thanks Alex, excited — budget is the main blocker for us, we need to know if this new assistant can run within about eighteen k a month for inference before we commit to infra.
[00:28] Kelsey Park: yeah that's our runway, also procurement needs a clear SOW and some cost sensitivity ranges.
[00:35] Samir Patel: great, we'll start with workload sizing — can you share typical session lengths, tokens per session, and peak concurrency? small questions are fine.
[00:42] Jamal Reed: typical session is chat-based, median 220 tokens per session, heavy ones up to 2k, about 6k unique active users/day, expected scale to 25k monthly active in quarter. Peak concurrency approx 60 concurrent requests, burst up to ~250 qps during crunch times.
[01:05] Alex Chen: good, so let's ballpark: if median is 220 tokens and 6k DAU, that's ~1.3M tokens/day or ~40M tokens/month. Kelsey does that align?
[01:16] Kelsey Park: yes that's the noisy estimate, though we might see seasonal spikes. For budgeting we should look at 40-60M tokens/mo.
[01:24] Samir Patel: ok. On model selection — for the POC do you want to test a lighter open model vs a higher quality one? We typically recommend two arms: 1) a cost-optimized quantized variant for throughput, 2) a higher-quality base for subjective eval.
[01:40] Maya Ortiz: quality is important, but we need to prove cost first. so start with the cost-optimized model and a smaller control group on higher-quality.
[01:48] Alex Chen: noted. Success criteria proposed: latency P95 under 250-300ms for short chats, cost not exceeding $0.00035 per token on average after batching and caching, and generation quality above baseline NPS — we'll put exact metrics in the SOW.
[02:05] Jamal Reed: that per-token number seems tight, how do you get there?
[02:09] Samir Patel: two levers: batching and KV/prefix caching. With continuous batching across concurrent requests we can amortize kernel overhead. Also prefix caching for repeated system prompts or common contexts can save up to 35-50% tokens on some workflows.
[02:26] Alex Chen: example: if we can batch to average batch size of 12-16 and cache 30% token reuse on average, effective token spend drops dramatically — we'll include model-level per-token estimates in the pricing worksheet.
[02:42] Kelsey Park: can you quantify numbers for us? even a rough calc helps procurement.
[02:48] Samir Patel: sure, rough example now: model raw cost ~ $0.0006/token (hosted for 13B Q4-style), batching factor 12 reduces kernel overhead equivalent to ~20% effective price reduction, caching 30% reduces billed tokens, overall effective cost could be ~ $0.00028-0.00034/token depending on seq length and hit rate. these are illustrative.
[03:14] Maya Ortiz: those are promising if true. how predictable are those savings though — we don't want variance wrecking our budget.
[03:21] Samir Patel: we'll run replay-style benchmarks with your sample prompts — that gives predictable estimates because it mirrors your real token distribution. Synthetic tests can over/underestimate.
[03:31] Alex Chen: for the POC we recommend a 2-week benchmark phase where we run replay at 1x, 5x traffic and measure P95 latency, throughput, and billed token counts with and without caching.
[03:44] Jamal Reed: about caching — our prompts include a lot of repeated system prompts and user patterns; what's the integration work for prefix/KV caching?
[03:52] Samir Patel: minimal SDK changes — you annotate the prompt pieces that are cacheable (system + certain embeddings) and the runtime manages KV cache. if you run private deployment it's still supported; for hosted we can enable and tune it.
[04:06] Kelsey Park: any implications for consistency or correctness? i'm worried cache staleness might return wrong context.
[04:12] Samir Patel: it's conservative by default: we only reuse if keys match exactly; we also version keys so you can invalidate on model update. we'll show logs in the console for hits/misses.
[04:22] Maya Ortiz: timeline? you said 2-week benchmark then POC — how long until we get results?
[04:28] Alex Chen: proposed POC timeline: week 0: SOW + infra prep; week 1-2: benchmark/replay runs; week 3: tune batching/caching + quality eval; week 4: final report and decision. total 4 weeks.
[04:40] Jamal Reed: do you need us to open ports or provide a dataset?
[04:44] Samir Patel: we need a representative prompt set (5-10k prompts ideally) and a sample traffic trace (session-level with token counts). for hosted testing we can run replay against a test model key — no ports required. for private or VPC we'll do architecture review.
[04:59] Kelsey Park: security: we need SOC2 + KMS integration — our legal expects customer-managed keys for PII in prompts.
[05:06] Alex Chen: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations in Private mode; hosted supports encrypted storage with bring-your-own-key for certain tiers. We'll surface the SOC2 artifacts and a KMS options doc.
[05:16] Maya Ortiz: procurement also asked about SLAs and fallbacks. if the model is down, we need automated fallback to a cheaper local model or degrade gracefully.
[05:25] Samir Patel: we support routing policies and automatic fallback to quantized variants or older pinned versions — those policies are part of the rollout config. we'll show examples in the Console.
[05:35] Kelsey Park: ok, for budgeting do you have a template or spreadsheet?
[05:38] Alex Chen: yes i'll attach a pricing worksheet that shows per-model raw cost, expected batching factor, caching hit rate scenarios (low/med/high), and projected monthly spend. we'll provide low/median/high scenarios for your 40-60M token range.
[05:52] Jamal Reed: benchmark metrics — which exact numbers will we collect?
[05:55] Samir Patel: P95 latency, mean latency, throughput (requests/sec), GPU utilization, billed tokens, cache hit/miss, cost-per-effective-token, and an ops log of any fallbacks/errors.
[06:08] Maya Ortiz: question on quantization — does it impact quality for our summarization use case?
[06:12] Samir Patel: small models and certain quantization formats can degrade some nuanced summarization quality; that's why we run a small human eval for quality. recommend a two-arm comparison with blind eval.
[06:24] Alex Chen: for decision gates: pass if cost within budget and quality delta <= 5% from baseline for the high-quality arm. We'll define exact metrics in the SOW.
[06:35] Kelsey Park: procurement timeline — we need SOW and pricing in 48 hours to hit next vendor review.
[06:40] Alex Chen: we'll prioritize that.
[06:42] Maya Ortiz: any risks i should flag to execs?
[06:45] Samir Patel: main risks are: 1) production token distribution differs significantly from sample prompts; 2) cache hit rates lower than expected; 3) unexpected spikes causing higher transient costs. mitigations: replay tests, conservative cache assumptions, and burst control policies.
[06:59] Jamal Reed: can we do an initial smoke run with 5k prompts on your infra this week?
[07:03] Samir Patel: yes, if you share 5k prompts today we can run a smoke and report back by Friday.
[07:09] Kelsey Park: and legal/security — we'll expect SOC2 docs and a short KMS integration note, please include in the pack.
[07:16] Alex Chen: will do.
[07:18] Priya Rao: quick note on observability — Console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdown, and traces; you'll be able to see exactly what prompts cost.
[07:26] Maya Ortiz: good, helps FinOps.
[07:28] Alex Chen: recap and next steps: 1) Alex send SOW + pricing worksheet by 4/24, 2) Samir share harness + run initial smoke by 4/29, 3) Cygnus share prompts and traffic profile by 4/27, 4) schedule architecture review for VPC/KMS the week of 4/30.
[07:46] Maya Ortiz: that works, thanks.
[07:48] Kelsey Park: thanks everyone.
[07:50] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the benchmark repo and security artifacts.
[48:00] Call ended

Action items and artifacts referenced: pilot SOW draft, pricing worksheet (batching/caching scenarios), benchmark harness repo (link to be shared), SOC2 and KMS integration doc.

Notes on transcription: Some jargon mis-heard ("KV cache" as "K-V cash" in one place), minor speaker overlaps.

End of transcript.
